newsitem.title: USA: Tenet raises credit facility to $2.8 bln.
newsitem.headline: Tenet raises credit facility to $2.8 bln.

text.p: Tenet HealthCare on Monday said it will increase the size of its new bank credit facility to $2.8 billion to complete the financing needs of the OrNda HealthCorp acquisition and future buyout targets.
The credit facility complements Tenet's $2.0 billion multi-tranche note offering priced via lead manager Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp on Monday.

The combined financing will allow Tenet to purchase $525 million in OrNda HealthCorp public debt, the $692.2 million existing OrNda credit facility and the $984 million existing Tenet credit facility, the company said.
Tenet said it will have $2.0 billion in remaining availability under the new credit facility for additional acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

"This increased borrowing capability supports Tenet's strategy of building strong integrated healthcare networks," said Jeffrey Barbakow, Tenet's chairman and chief executive officer. "Our ability to pursue strategic acquisitions and other business opportunities will be significantly increased."
Tenet said it expects to complete its acquisition of OrNda in a tax-free stock transaction by January 30. The deal is valued at more than $1.8 billion.
